lines.text: The lamps were finished in the last week of winter. Twenty-one, in fact. Tobin made an extra one, for luck.
Pell's sleigh came and went. Four thousand two hundred crowns, in gold and Vaskan notes, locked in a chest in my bedroom. Ash slept on top of it.
The snow began to soften. Then the river ice cracked. First thaw.
And with it, House Corrow.
Thirty riders came up the north road, with crows on their banners. And at their head, a thin man with a thin smile.
Lord Lucan Varr? I am Steward Corvin, of House Corrow. I'm here to collect a debt. Or, failing that, to collect Greyhollow.
Four thousand crowns, due at first thaw. It's all here. Count it.
He counted it. Slowly. Every coin. Then his smile grew wider.
Four thousand crowns. Excellent. And the interest?
What interest?
Clause nine. Interest at twenty parts in a hundred, added every season. You owe eight thousand, my lord.
He held up the contract. The ink of clause nine was a little darker than the rest.
I had read that contract a hundred times on the road north. There was no clause nine.
That clause is a forgery. The ink is fresh. Your scribe didn't even match the hand.
A serious accusation, from a boy with no rings. Who will the court believe? House Corrow, or the zero of House Varr?
Behind him, thirty riders put their hands on their swords. Not Corrow men. Sellswords, paid to do what a lord's own men can't be seen doing.
My lord. Thirty sellswords. Professionals. We have thirty-seven farmers.
I looked at my farmers. Tobin, with his hammer. Wren, with her bow. Bram, with his one arm and his old sword. And Ash, the size of a horse, showing his teeth.
I didn't know then what I know now. But I remember thinking, very clearly: they don't look like farmers anymore.
Steward Corvin. You have your four thousand crowns. Take them, and leave my land.
Or what?
Or I find out what thirty-seven farmers can do.
Kill the dog first.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter eight, coming soon.
